input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us, which is the preferred position. Section 12.3 goes further and expressly preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service and to operate in any field or territory, and records that we have given no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment — a provision that benefits us and should not be touched. A text scan found no "shall not develop/market/sell", "competing products" or territory restraints binding us: the only competition-related references are Section 24.2 (limiting Vendor's ability to assign to our competitor, in our favour) and Section 13.4 (ordinary acceptable-use restrictions on reverse engineering and misuse of the Services, not a restraint on our business). The exclusivity language in Section 2.2 is a restraint-type term but is assessed under the EXCLUSIVITY rule, so we do not flag it again here.
